fullPassage: Economists like teaching about taxes and subsidies because they don't "stick" where they "land". Some of a tax's burden or a subsidy's benefit passes from those who write or cash the check to other market participants because taxes and subsidies change people's behavior. Buyers might bear the brunt of a tax legally paid by sellers and vice versa. Who is legally responsible for writing the check doesn't matter. How suppliers and demanders respond to changing prices does. Cigarette buyers tend to be less price-sensitive than sellers. When large tobacco companies get taxed, the cigarette supply shrinks. Smokers pay higher prices, but most don't cut back much because they aren't especially price-sensitive. Cigarette taxes land on huge corporations with a great amount of cash but stick to disproportionately poor smokers.

Some of a tax's burden or a subsidy's benefit passes from those who write or cash the check to other market participants because taxes and subsidies change people's behavior. Buyers might bear the brunt of a tax legally paid by sellers and vice versa. Who is legally responsible for writing the check doesn't matter. How suppliers and demanders respond to changing prices does. Cigarette buyers tend to be less price-sensitive than sellers. When large tobacco companies get taxed, the cigarette supply shrinks. Smokers pay higher prices, but most don't cut back much because they aren't especially price-sensitive. Cigarette taxes land on huge corporations with a great amount of cash but stick to disproportionately poor smokers.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>they</u>가 가리키는 대상으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① smokers: 바로 앞 Smokers를 지칭. most의 선행사 역할.
❌ ② sellers: 판매자는 앞 문장에서 비교 대상.
❌ ③ large tobacco companies: 담배 회사는 과세 대상.
❌ ④ cigarette buyers: 이미 첫 문장에서 언급된 별개의 표현.
